nodes.description: Brachydactyly of all the tubular bones, with a consistent wavy metacarpophalangeal pattern profile in both published families. The distribution differs between them: foot-predominant with mild hand involvement in the Slovenian kindred, hand-only with radiographically normal feet in the second family.

evidence.snippet: revealed a consistent wavy pattern with brachydactyly of all tubular bones with marked shortening of the first and third distal phalanges, second middle phalanx and first proximal phalanx

evidence.snippet: mild hand involvement (short distal, middle, proximal phalanges and clinodactyly)

nodes.description: Progressive loss of sinoatrial and atrioventricular conduction tissue with myocardial fibrosis and contractile failure. The clinical course is characteristically adult-onset and progressive, running from sinus node disease and AV block through atrial and ventricular tachyarrhythmia to dilated cardiomyopathy and sudden death.

nodes.description: Shortening of the tubular bones of the hands and feet, with a characteristic wavy metacarpophalangeal pattern profile and disproportionate involvement of the distal phalanges. How a nuclear lamina defect produces this is unknown, and it is the genuinely novel part of the phenotype. The one available clue is comparative: acro-osteolysis occurs in other LMNA disorders, and the distal-predominant shortening in both heart-hand families points the same way, suggesting the distal limb elements are the ones sensitive to LMNA dosage. The foot-versus-hand difference between the two families is unexplained.

evidence.reference_title: Heart-hand syndrome IV: a second family with LMNA-related cardiomyopathy and brachydactyly.
evidence.snippet: The more severe involvement of the distal phalanges seen in both families and acro-osteolysis seen in other LMNA patients suggests an increased susceptibility of the distal limb elements to disturbances in LMNA dosage.

evidence.reference_title: Heart-hand syndrome of Slovenian type: a new kind of laminopathy.
evidence.snippet: This LMNA mutation segregates with a new type of heart-hand syndrome in a previously reported family suffering from adult onset progressive conduction system disease, atrial and ventricular tachyarrhythmias, sudden death, dilated cardiomyopathy, and brachydactyly with predominant foot involvement.

evidence.reference_title: Heart-hand syndrome IV: a second family with LMNA-related cardiomyopathy and brachydactyly.
evidence.snippet: a heterozygous C>T missense variant in exon 6 as the primary mutation for both the cardiac and limb phenotypes

nodes.description: A heterozygous LMNA variant yielding an abnormal lamin A/C protein. The two published families reach this node by different routes: a cryptic splice-site change producing a frameshifted, truncated protein demonstrated in patient fibroblasts, and an exon 6 missense change. Lamin A/C is a type V intermediate filament protein forming the meshwork that underlies the inner nuclear membrane.

nodes.description: Nuclear damage is translated into myocardial dysfunction partly through MAPK hyperactivation, with the ERK, JNK and p38 branches all raised in the Lmna H222P mouse. This arm is separated from the WNT arm below because the two move in opposite directions - MAPK up, WNT down - and a single node cannot carry one `modifier`. It is also the arm with a drug: the p38 inhibitor in trials targets this node, not the WNT one.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of ARRY-371797 in LMNA-Related Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Phase 2 Study.
evidence.snippet: p38 MAPK pathway activation has also been demonstrated in biopsies from the hearts of adult patients with LMNA-related DCM

evidence.reference_title: Role of Lamin A/C Gene Mutations in the Signaling Defects Leading to Cardiomyopathies.
evidence.snippet: The mechanisms by which expression of LmnaH222P leads to ERK1/2 signaling hyperactivation are under investigation.

nodes.description: In contracting cardiomyocytes the fragile nucleus is damaged, and the force that damages it comes from the microtubule cage encircling the nucleus rather than from contractile strain transmitted through the LINC complex. That distinction is experimentally established and is counterintuitive: disrupting the LINC complex helps not by uncoupling contraction from the nucleus but by eliminating the microtubule cage. The work was done in lamin A/C-deficient models, not in this disease's variant, so the step is inferred for this entity.

evidence.reference_title: Microtubule forces drive nuclear damage in LMNA cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Computational modeling revealed that microtubule forces create local stress concentrations that damage lamin A/C-deficient nuclei.

evidence.reference_title: Microtubule forces drive nuclear damage in LMNA cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: Microtubule disruption prevented nuclear damage and preserved cardiac function in lamin A/C deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Microtubule forces drive nuclear damage in LMNA cardiomyopathy.
evidence.snippet: The LINC complex was mostly dispensable for transferring contractile strain to the nucleus, and its disruption did not rescue elevated nuclear strain in lamin A/C-deficient cardiomyocytes.

nodes.description: The arm most directly relevant to this disease's defining conduction phenotype. WNT/beta-catenin is reduced in LMNA cardiomyopathy with reduced connexin 43, the gap junction the conduction phenotype runs through, and pharmacological reactivation improves both contractility and intraventricular conduction in the mouse model. Separated from the MAPK node above because the two arms move in opposite directions.

evidence.reference_title: Decreased WNT/beta-catenin signalling contributes to the pathogenesis of dilated cardiomyopathy caused by mutations in the lamin a/C gene.
evidence.snippet: Hearts of LmnaH222P/H222P mice also demonstrated lowered expression of the gap junction connexin 43.

nodes.description: Disproportionate shortening of the distal phalanges, most marked in the first and third digits. This distal predominance is shared by both families and is the one feature with a proposed mechanistic reading.

nodes.description: The outcome that makes early molecular diagnosis and cascade testing of relatives the point of recognising this syndrome. In the second family sudden death occurred at age 23.

Bound to the supraventricular tachycardia term because the sources say "atrial tachyarrhythmias" without naming a specific rhythm, so no narrower term (atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter) is asserted.

nodes.description: The lamina meshwork is weakened and the nuclear envelope structurally abnormal, which is demonstrated in fibroblasts from this disease's own patients rather than only inferred from LMNA biology generally. This is the shared upstream lesion for both the cardiac and the skeletal arm, and the point at which they diverge.

evidence.reference_title: Heart-hand syndrome of Slovenian type: a new kind of laminopathy.
evidence.snippet: nuclear envelope abnormalities confirming that this LMNA mutation is pathogenic

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variant in exon 6, segregating with both the cardiac and the limb phenotype in the second family. Previously published in patients with LMNA cardiac disease in whom limb anomalies were not reported, including one with acro-osteolysis.

evidence.reference_title: Heart-hand syndrome IV: a second family with LMNA-related cardiomyopathy and brachydactyly.
evidence.snippet: Patients with LMNA c.1003C>T (p.Arg335Trp) and cardiac disease have been published; however, limb anomalies were not reported

nodes.description: Intronic change creating a cryptic splice acceptor, so that 11 intronic nucleotides are retained in the mRNA and the resulting frameshift yields a truncated lamin A/C protein. This was the allele in the original Slovenian kindred, and the first demonstration of a truncated lamin A/C protein in patient cells.

evidence.reference_title: Heart-hand syndrome of Slovenian type: a new kind of laminopathy.
evidence.snippet: We report a new LMNA mutation (c.1609-12T>G, IVS9-12 T>G) that creates a new cryptic splicing site with the retention of 11 intronic nucleotides in the mRNA.

evidence.reference_title: Heart-hand syndrome of Slovenian type: a new kind of laminopathy.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the fibroblasts of two affected family members identified for the first time a truncated lamin A/C protein resulting from the frame shift created by the new splicing site, together with nuclear envelope abnormalities confirming that this LMNA mutation is pathogenic.

nodes.description: An investigational disease-modifying approach targeting the MAPK arm of the signalling cascade downstream of nuclear damage. The oral selective p38 inhibitor ARRY-371797 was studied in a phase 2 open-label trial in LMNA-related dilated cardiomyopathy. Included here because it is the first therapy aimed at the mechanism rather than its consequences, and because it illustrates that the signalling arm of this pathograph is the druggable one; it is not established therapy, and no patient with this heart-hand syndrome has been reported on it.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and Safety of ARRY-371797 in LMNA-Related Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Phase 2 Study.
evidence.snippet: This phase 2 study assessed the effects of the oral selective p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase inhibitor ARRY-371797 on functional capacity and cardiac function in patients with LMNA-related dilated cardiomyopathy.
